title: Comparing — more, most, and just the same
goal: Compare two things, name the best (or worst), and build new adjectives yourself with three Persian prefixes.
bekal: use ـترین before a noun for "the most …"
build your own adjectives with بی‌، با‌، and پر‌

dialogs.title: گفتگو — اصفهان یا شیراز؟
dialogs.intro: Budi has four days off and can't decide where to go. Maryam has strong opinions.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: چهار روز تعطیلم. اصفهان بهتر است یا شیراز؟
lines.baca: chahâr ruz ta'tilam. Esfahân behtar ast yâ Shirâz?
lines.id: I have four days off. Is Isfahan better, or Shiraz?
lines.literal: four day off-I-am. Isfahan better is or Shiraz?

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.text: سؤالِ سختی است! اصفهان بزرگ‌تر از شیراز است.
lines.baca: so'âl-e sakhti ast! Esfahân bozorgtar az Shirâz ast.
lines.id: That's a hard question! Isfahan is bigger than Shiraz.
lines.literal: question-of hard-a is! Isfahan bigger from Shiraz is.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.id: Shiraz. But Isfahan's buildings are more beautiful.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.text: بله. یکی از بزرگ‌ترین میدان‌هایِ دنیا است.
lines.baca: bale. yeki az bozorgtarin meydânhâ-ye donyâ ast.
lines.id: Yes. It's one of the biggest squares in the world.
lines.literal: yes. one from biggest squares-of world is.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.text: آرامگاهِ حافظ، باغ‌هایِ قدیمی، و تختِ جمشید نزدیک است.
lines.baca: ârâmgâh-e Hâfez, bâghhâ-ye ghadimi, va Takht-e Jamshid nazdik ast.
lines.id: Hafez's tomb, old gardens, and Persepolis is close by.
lines.literal: tomb-of Hafez, gardens-of old, and Throne-of Jamshid near is.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: کدام ارزان‌تر است؟ پولم زیاد نیست.
lines.baca: kodâm arzântar ast? pulam ziyâd nist.
lines.id: Which one is cheaper? I don't have much money.
lines.literal: which cheaper is? money-my much is-not.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.text: شیراز کمی ارزان‌تر است و هوایش هم بهتر است.
lines.baca: Shirâz kami arzântar ast va havâyash ham behtar ast.
lines.id: Shiraz is a bit cheaper, and its weather is better too.
lines.literal: Shiraz a-little cheaper is and air-its also better is.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: پس شیراز. سفر تا آنجا چقدر طول می‌کشد؟
lines.baca: pas Shirâz. safar tâ ânjâ cheghadr tul mikeshad?
lines.id: Shiraz, then. How long does the trip there take?
lines.literal: so Shiraz. trip up-to there how-much length pulls-it?

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.text: با هواپیما یک ساعت، با اتوبوس دوازده ساعت.
lines.baca: bâ havâpeymâ yek sâ'at, bâ otobus davâzdah sâ'at.
lines.id: One hour by plane, twelve hours by bus.
lines.literal: with plane one hour, with bus twelve hour.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: هواپیما سریع‌تر، ولی اتوبوس ارزان‌تر است.
lines.baca: havâpeymâ sari'tar, vali otobus arzântar ast.
lines.id: The plane is faster, but the bus is cheaper.
lines.literal: plane faster, but bus cheaper is.

lines.speaker: مریم:
lines.text: اتوبوس‌هایِ ایران راحت‌ترین اتوبوس‌هایِ دنیا هستند. باور کنید!
lines.baca: otobushâ-ye Irân râhattarin otobushâ-ye donyâ hastand. bâvar konid!
lines.id: Iran's buses are the most comfortable buses in the world. Believe me!
lines.literal: buses-of Iran most-comfortable buses-of world are-they. belief do-you!

notes: ⚠️ **"More … than" uses از, not که.** بزرگ‌تر **از** شیراز = "bigger than Shiraz". The most common mistake is using که ("that") because it feels like "than" — but Persian uses the word for "from", just like Arabic (**من**). Think "bigger *from* Shiraz".

⚠️ **The ending ـترین stands BEFORE its noun, and it's the only adjective that does.** بزرگ‌ترین میدان ("the biggest square"), راحت‌ترین اتوبوس ("the most comfortable bus"), بهترین رستوران ("the best restaurant"). All of unit 3 taught you that adjectives come after the noun; the "most" form is the exception, and it takes **no** ezafe.
**"One of the …-est" = یکی از بزرگ‌ترین ….** A very common, easy pattern: یکی از ("one of") + ترین + plural noun. یکی از بهترین دوستانم ("one of my best friends").
**The form زیباترند = زیباتر + ـند.** The plural "are" ending attaches straight to the comparative adjective. It's the same use as خوبم in unit 1 — no new rule.
**"It takes (time)" = طول می‌کشد**, literally "it pulls length". چقدر طول می‌کشد؟ ("how long does it take?") is one of the questions you'll need most when traveling.

**Spoken forms:** کدوم بهتره؟ (*kodum behtare?*), ارزون‌تره (*arzuntare*), چقدر طول می‌کشه؟ (*cheghadr tul mikeshe?*). Notice again the ân → un shift that hits almost every word: ارزان → ارزون، کدام → کدوم، نان → نون.

grammars.title: The endings ـتر and ـترین
after: **Four irregular adjectives** — and all four are used constantly:
Note that بیشتر and کمتر are also used as words on their own: بیشتر مردم ("most people"), کمتر از ده ("less than ten").

grammars.title: Comparison sentence patterns
after: For **sameness**, use مثلِ ("like") or به اندازهٔ ("as big as, as much as"), not ـتر.
To strengthen a comparison, add خیلی or کمی, e.g. خیلی بهتر از … ("much better than"), کمی ارزان‌تر ("a little cheaper").

grammars.title: Three prefixes that build adjectives for you
body: Persian builds adjectives from nouns with three very productive prefixes. Once you recognize them, hundreds of words open up on their own — much like English -less, -ful, and with-.
after: **The prefix بی works like English "-less"** — بی‌ادب is literally "manner-less". You can attach بی to many other nouns too, and the meaning usually comes out exactly as you'd guess.

You can use these prefixes yourself to guess meanings: بی‌فایده ("useless"), بی‌صبر ("impatient"), باتجربه ("experienced"), پرکار ("full of work" = hardworking). When you meet an unfamiliar word starting with بی، با، or پر, cut off the prefix and the meaning usually pops right out.

blocks.text: Look at the pair **راحت / ناراحت**: the prefix نا ("not") flips an adjective's meaning, just like English "un-". More examples: امید ("hope") → ناامید ("hopeless"), درست ("right") → نادرست ("wrong"), کافی ("enough") → ناکافی ("not enough").

blocks.title: Two words from Arabic: معروف and مشهور
items: Both mean "famous" and were borrowed from Arabic. Persian is full of Arabic loanwords — if you know any Arabic, Urdu, or Turkish, you already half-know thousands of Persian words.

More examples that are easy to spot: کتاب، قلم، وقت، حال، سلام، دنیا، خبر، عالم، صبر، شکر، فکر، عادت، لازم، مهم، ممکن، مشکل. When a Persian word looks familiar from one of those languages, trust it — it's most likely the same word.

blocks.title: Four sentences for planning a trip
items: "Which is better, ... or ...?" — کدام بهتر است، ... یا ...؟
"How long does it take?" — چقدر طول می‌کشد؟
"What's the cheapest way?" — ارزان‌ترین راه چیست؟
"What must I see?" — چه چیزی را حتماً باید ببینم؟ This last question will get you a long list, two cups of tea, and most likely an offer to show you around.
The bus is cheaper, but the plane is faster.
This is the best restaurant in town.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: اصفهان بزرگ‌تر از شیراز است. — این از آن بهتر است. — او از من جوان‌تر است. — اتوبوس ارزان‌تر است، ولی هواپیما سریع‌تر است. — این بهترین رستورانِ شهر است.
اصفهان بزرگ‌تر از شیراز است. — اتوبوس ارزان‌تر است. — این بهترین رستورانِ شهر است. — چقدر طول می‌کشد؟ — او از من جوان‌تر است.
